next_state_election.name: State Election
next_state_election.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Election Calendars

glance_notes.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — November 3, 2026 State Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Early Voting: Early voting for Connecticut's November 3, 2026 State Election runs from October 19 through November 1, 2026. Standard hours are 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with extended hours from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on October 27 and October 29.

glance_notes.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — 2026 Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Beginning in 2026, any eligible active registered Connecticut voter may request and vote an absentee ballot without providing a specific reason or excuse.

glance_notes.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Same-Day Registration
glance_notes.text: Same-Day Registration: For regular general elections, Connecticut provides Same-Day Registration during the early-voting period and on Election Day. Same-Day Registration is not available for primaries or special elections.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Connecticut residents can register to vote online through the Connecticut Secretary of the State or submit a paper voter registration application. You are eligible to register if you are a United States citizen living in Connecticut, are at least 17 and will turn 18 on or before Election Day, and, if you were convicted of a felony that affected your voting rights, have completed confinement as required by Connecticut law. Your application must be approved by your local registrar of voters before you are registered.
register.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Online Voter Registration
register.internal_note: Supplemental verification sources: Connecticut Secretary of the State Voting Eligibility — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/voting-eligibility](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/voting-eligibility) — establishes citizenship, Connecticut residence, age and felony-confinement eligibility requirements. Connecticut Secretary of the State Voter Registration Application — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/register-to-vote/voter-registration-application-english-and-spanish](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/register-to-vote/voter-registration-application-english-and-spanish) — confirms paper registration and that an applicant is not registered until the registrar approves the application.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Connecticut's official voter lookup tool to check whether you are registered and review your current voter registration information. The same official lookup can help identify your Election Day polling place.
check_registration.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Voter Registration Lookup
check_registration.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: Connecticut Secretary of the State Voter Registration Information — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/voter-registration-information](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/voter-registration-information) — expressly directs voters to the official voter lookup tool to check current registration status.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Connecticut's regular pre-election voter registration cutoff is 18 days before an election. Eligible voters who miss the regular deadline for a general election can use Same-Day Registration during the early-voting period or on Election Day. Same-Day Registration is not available for primaries or special elections. To use Same-Day Registration, you must register and vote at your town's designated Same-Day Registration location and provide the required proof of identity and residence.
deadlines.glance_value: 18 days before election; SDR available for general elections
deadlines.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Voter Registration Information
deadlines.internal_note: Additional verification source: Connecticut Secretary of the State Same-Day Registration — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-day-registration/election-day-registration](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-day-registration/election-day-registration) — establishes the 18-day cutoff and availability of SDR during early voting and Election Day for regular general elections. The Secretary of the State's 2026 early-voting page expressly states SDR is unavailable for primaries and special elections.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Connecticut's official Voter Registration Lookup and Election Polling Place Locator to find your Election Day polling place. Early-voting locations are separate and are published by the Secretary of the State by city and town. Same-Day Registration also takes place at designated locations rather than at a voter's ordinary Election Day polling place.
polling_place.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Voter Registration Lookup and Polling Place Locator
polling_place.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: Connecticut Secretary of the State Where and How Do I Vote — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/where-and-how-do-i-vote](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/where-and-how-do-i-vote) — links the official polling-place locator and separate early-voting locations. Same-Day Registration source: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-day-registration/election-day-registration](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-day-registration/election-day-registration).

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Registered Connecticut voters can vote at their assigned polling place on Election Day. Polls for elections and primaries are open from 6:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., and anyone standing in line at 8:00 p.m. is allowed to vote. For a regular general election, an eligible person who needs to register or who moved to another Connecticut town can instead use the town's designated Same-Day Registration location to register and vote.
election_day.glance_value: Vote at your assigned polling place
election_day.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Where and How Do I Vote
election_day.internal_note: Primary source establishes Election Day polling-place lookup, 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. hours and protection for voters in line at 8:00 p.m. Supplemental source for Same-Day Registration eligibility and location: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-day-registration/election-day-registration](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-day-registration/election-day-registration).

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: For Connecticut elections and primaries, polls are open from 6:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Any eligible voter standing in line at the polls at 8:00 p.m. is allowed to cast a ballot. Referendum voting hours can vary by town, so voters should check with their town clerk for a referendum.
polling_hours.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Where and How Do I Vote
polling_hours.internal_note: The Secretary of the State directly states the 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. election and primary hours, the protection for electors standing in line at 8:00 p.m., and the referendum exception requiring voters to check local hours.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Connecticut provides in-person early voting before statewide elections and primaries. For the November 3, 2026 State Election, early voting runs from Monday, October 19 through Sunday, November 1. Early-voting locations are open from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. each day except Tuesday, October 27 and Thursday, October 29, when extended hours are 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Early-voting locations are published by the Secretary of the State for each city and town.
early_voting.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — November 3, 2026 State Election Calendar
early_voting.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar directly establishes the October 19-November 1 early-voting period, standard 10:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. hours, and 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. extended hours on October 27 and 29, citing Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 9-163aa(a)(1)(B) and 9-174(c)(1). Official 2026 location source: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/early-voting/early-voting-locations---2026](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/early-voting/early-voting-locations---2026).

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Connecticut now allows any eligible active registered voter to request and vote an absentee ballot without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 State Election, the online absentee-ballot request portal opens September 19, absentee ballots begin being issued October 2, and the deadline to request an absentee ballot is November 2. Voters may request a ballot through the state's online portal or submit an official paper application to their town clerk. Completed absentee ballots must be received by the appropriate town clerk by the close of polls on Election Day to be counted.
absentee_mail.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — 2026 Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: This is a significant 2026 change. Public Act 26-42 implemented the November 2024 constitutional amendment expanding absentee voting. The Secretary of the State's current 2026 page expressly states that voters no longer need a specific reason or excuse and provides the September 19 portal opening, October 2 issuance date and November 2 request deadline for the November 3 election. Supplemental verification source for administration and ballot receipt: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/absentee-ballot-process](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/absentee-ballot-process). Because this is newly implemented law, reverify frequently.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Connecticut does not generally require a photo ID to vote. At the polling place, most registered voters are asked to present either a Social Security card or another preprinted form of identification showing their name and address, name and signature, or name and photograph. A voter who does not have one of these documents may generally sign a statement under penalty of false statement confirming that they are the voter whose name appears on the official checklist. Different federal identification rules can apply to certain first-time voters who registered by mail and did not previously provide the required identifying information. Same-Day Registration has separate proof-of-identity and residence requirements.
voter_id.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Voter Rights and Identification
voter_id.internal_note: Official Secretary of the State voter-ID material under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 9-261 establishes Social Security card/preprinted-ID options and the signed-statement alternative. Secretary of the State Where and How Do I Vote — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/where-and-how-do-i-vote](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/where-and-how-do-i-vote) — explicitly states that photo identification is not generally required. Supplemental federal first-time voter source: Connecticut Secretary of the State HAVA page — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/hava/help-america-vote-act-of-2002](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/hava/help-america-vote-act-of-2002). Same-Day Registration proof requirements are distinct and documented at [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-day-registration/election-day-registration](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-day-registration/election-day-registration).

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Connecticut provides accessible voting equipment at every polling place. The accessible ballot-marking system allows voters to make selections privately and independently using options including a touchscreen, audio interface, tactile keys and customizable displays. The system marks the same paper ballot used by other voters, which can then be placed through the optical-scan tabulator. Connecticut also provides voting-rights information and absentee-ballot accommodations for voters with disabilities.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment at every polling place
accessible_voting.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Where and How Do I Vote
accessible_voting.internal_note: Primary source directly establishes that an accessible ballot-marking device is available at every polling place and describes touchscreen, audio, tactile-key and customizable-display accessibility features. Additional official accessibility resource: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/accessible-voting](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/accessible-voting).

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Connecticut military and overseas voters can request an absentee ballot using Connecticut's absentee-ballot application or the Federal Post Card Application. A Federal Post Card Application can cover both the primary and general election ballots for the year. Voters can request delivery electronically or by standard mail. Eligible uniformed-service members, merchant mariners and qualifying spouses or dependents may also use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup if a requested regular ballot does not arrive in time. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot must reach the appropriate local Connecticut election official no later than the close of polls on Election Day.
military_overseas.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The current official page directly supports Connecticut absentee application and FPCA use, electronic or postal delivery options, FWAB availability for specified UOCAVA voters, Election Day receipt requirement for FWAB, and return of applications to the voter's municipal clerk. The page is currently marked by the Secretary of the State as being updated, so this section should be rechecked more frequently.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student living away from home may choose to vote in their hometown or register to vote in the Connecticut town where they live while attending college, provided they meet Connecticut's voter eligibility requirements. A Connecticut student attending college away from home can also vote through Connecticut's absentee-ballot process if eligible and registered in their Connecticut hometown.
student_voting.glance_value: Vote at home or register in your college town
student_voting.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Student Voter Fact Sheet
student_voting.internal_note: The official Student Voter Fact Sheet directly states that a college student can vote in the hometown or in the town where the student lives while at college. Supplemental verification source: Voting Eligibility — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/voting-eligibility](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/voting-eligibility) — independently states the same student choice. Absentee rules changed in 2026 to no-excuse absentee voting, so the reader-facing wording avoids reproducing the older fact sheet's now-superseded excuse list.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: The Connecticut Secretary of the State publishes official town-by-town sample ballots for elections when they become available. Because ballot contents depend on where you live, use the Secretary of the State's current sample-ballot resource and select your municipality to review the appropriate ballot.
sample_ballot.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — MyVote.CT.gov Voter Resources
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of the State's current voter resource page provides the official Town-by-Town Sample Ballots service. As of August 30, 2026, the November 3 General Election sample ballots are not yet presented as a completed statewide set on the main voter page; the 2026 Voter Guide is also marked 'coming soon.' This section describes the official process without claiming the November ballots are already posted.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Connecticut Secretary of the State, Legislation and Election Administration Division, State Office Building, 165 Capitol Avenue, Suite 1000, Hartford, CT 06106. Election questions: 860-509-6100. Email: vote@ct.gov. The Secretary of the State's general business hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Connecticut elections are also administered locally by town clerks and registrars of voters.
contact.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: Official Contact Us page verifies the State Office Building address, business hours, LEAD phone number 860-509-6100 and LEAD email [lead@ct.gov](mailto:lead@ct.gov). The Secretary of the State Election Questions page — [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-services/election-questions](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-services/election-questions) — specifically directs voter election questions to [vote@ct.gov](mailto:vote@ct.gov) or 860-509-6100. LEAD description: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-services/what-is-the-legislation-and-elections-administration--division-lead](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/election-services/what-is-the-legislation-and-elections-administration--division-lead).

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use MyVote.CT.gov and the Connecticut Secretary of the State's Elections and Voting resources for statewide voter information, registration, polling-place lookup, early-voting locations, absentee voting, sample ballots and election dates. Connecticut elections are administered jointly with local officials, including registrars of voters and town clerks. The Secretary of the State provides an official directory for contacting local election officials.
official_resources.source_name: Connecticut Secretary of the State — MyVote.CT.gov
official_resources.internal_note: Official registration information: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/voter-registration-information](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/voter-registration-information). Official polling and voting information: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/where-and-how-do-i-vote](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/where-and-how-do-i-vote). Official early-voting information: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/early-voting/early-voting](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/early-voting/early-voting). Official absentee information: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/absentee-voting](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/voter-information/absentee-voting). Official election calendars: [https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/calendars/election-calendars](https://portal.ct.gov/sots/election-services/calendars/election-calendars). The current voter resource page provides Local Officials Contact Information.
